text:
Priya (AE): Quick sync on ACME POC — they want a short 2-week eval for realtime doc-summarization. Need: success criteria, capacity estimate, and a conservative budget. They said peak ~500 req/min, avg 60 tokens/output, 95th latency <300ms.

Alex (Sales Eng): Got it. Do we have their prompt set size / eval corpus? also are these requests single-turn or multi-turn?

Priya (AE): Single-turn summarization of single-doc inputs. They can share ~200 gold prompts + 50 adversarial edge cases.

Maria (Solutions): Clarifying: are they doing streaming output or full-block response? streaming would change latency/cost profile. Also do they need embeddings or only generation?

Priya (AE): Generation only, streaming OK but not required. No embeddings for POC.

Devon (ML Eng): Quick calc: 500 req/min -> 8.3 req/s -> 8.3 * 60 tokens = 500 tokens/s sustained. If we target 95th latency <300ms per request, batching window is tiny. Streaming helps amortize but increases tail.

Kai (Infra): For throughput/latency tradeoffs: options
- Option A (single-dedicated GPU, lowest infra ops): 1x A100 or H100 serving optimized 13B quant model. With optimized kernels, realistic sustained throughput ~600-800 tok/s but tail depends on concurrency. Should meet 500 tok/s with conservative headroom.
- Option B (redundant small fleet): 2x GPUs autoscaled -> better isolation for spikes, allows rolling deploys; higher monthly cost.

Alex (Sales Eng): Do we have a per-token cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated for this workload? Need to present rough $/day for the buyer.

Devon (ML Eng): Ballpark numbers (POC-level):
- Model: rw-13b-quant (recommended for latency/cost)
- Tokens per request: 60 out * assume 10 prompt tokens -> 70 tokens total
- 500 req/min -> 35k tokens/min -> 2100k tokens/hour -> 50k tokens/day (wait recalc)

Devon (ML Eng): Sorry small math fix: 500 req/min * 70 tokens = 35,000 tokens/min. *60 = 2,100,000 tokens/hour. For a 24h run that's ~50.4M tokens/day. For a 2-week POC, assume 50% duty cycle -> ~25M tokens/day peak window for billing.

Alex (Sales Eng): Good catch. So rough hosted metered cost at $0.00005 per token (example) -> 50.4M * 0.00005 = $2,520/day. Dedicated reserved GPU pricing spreads differently — infra + infra rental ~ $400-$900/day depending on contract/region.

Maria (Solutions): We should present 3 scenarios to the customer: conservative (single GPU dedicated w/ reserved), performance (2 GPU autoscale), and hosted (metered). Each with success criteria and risk.

Priya (AE): Success criteria proposal: 1) 95th latency <300ms on 80% of the eval set (200 curated prompts). 2) Summaries reach ROUGE-F1 >= baseline + manual review pass on 20 random samples. 3) No more than 1% request error rate during peak. 4) Security/contract checklist signed (we'll hand wave on that but need to push security questionnaire).

Devon (ML Eng): For evals: ask ACME to label 200 prompts with expected summary length and 20 adversarial edge cases. We'll run automatic metrics + 1-2 human reviewers for qualitative pass. Dev plan: setup eval harness (1 day), ingest prompts (0.5 day), run baseline and 3 model configs (1 day), tune batching/quant settings (1-2 days).

Kai (Infra): Timeline for infra: provisioning dedicated node (if reserved) ~ 2 business days; if hosted our endpoints are immediate. For on-prem/private they asked about VPC — that'll add 3-5 days for networking + security review.

Priya (AE): Budget ask from buyer is $3k/day cap for POC. Can we present a recommended configuration that fits under that?

Alex (Sales Eng): Under $3k/day hosted cost estimate we might need to recommend: reduce concurrency windows, use rw-13b-quant, and enable prefix caching for repeated context. Also propose a staged run: peak-load validation only for 2 hours/day instead of continuous 24h.

Devon (ML Eng): Technical recs to save cost: 1) lower max tokens output to target 40-60 2) enable KV/prefix cache if many repeated doc types 3) use quantized 13B vs 34B 4) tune batching to ~16-32 depending on latency.

Maria (Solutions): I'll draft the POC one-pager: objectives, eval plan, infra options with cost bands, and ask list (prompts + security contact + expected traffic pattern). Can share by EOD.

Priya (AE): Actions: Maria to draft POC one-pager; Devon to prepare eval harness + baseline config; Kai to produce 2 infra cost options (dedicated vs hosted) with daily numbers; Alex to align pricing talking points. We meet tomorrow 10am PT to finalize.

OpsBot: Reminder set: #poc-acme-review tomorrow 10:00 PT (link) :bell:

Priya (AE): Thanks team — will ping ACME to confirm prompt export and security contact.

Alex (Sales Eng): 👍 will prep the cost comparison table and example SLO clause for the POC contract.
